text: Coca-Cola is one of the most iconic global brands, and it has an extensive product portfolio that spans across several categories. The company’s most recognized product is Coca-Cola (regular), but it also offers Diet Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, catering to health- conscious consumers who prefer a low-calorie or sugar-free option. In the soft drinks category, Coca-Cola also includes Sprite, a popular lemon-lime soda, and Fanta, which comes in multiple fruit flavors like Orange, Grape, and Strawberry. Moving into the energy drinks segment, Coca-Cola owns Monster Energy, a leading global brand with various flavors including Monster Energy Zero Ultra, Monster Energy Green, and Monster Energy Assault. In the water category, Coca-Cola offers Dasani (a purified bottled water) and Smartwater (premium vapor-distilled water). The brand is also present in juices with Minute Maid and Simply Orange, offering a range of fruit juices like orange, apple, and pomegranate, as well as Minute Maid Pulpy and Minute Maid Fresh. In the tea segment, Coca-Cola offers Gold Peak and Honest Tea, with a variety of options ranging from sweetened iced tea to organic, low- calorie beverages. Coca-Cola has a significant presence in sports drinks with Powerade, which comes in flavors like Fruit Punch and Mountain Berry Blast. The company also markets ready-to-drink coffee through brands like Costa Coffee and Georgia Coffee, with variants like Costa Espresso and Costa Latte. Additionally, Coca-Cola has ventured into the plant-based beverage market with AdeZ, offering a range of smoothies made with ingredients like fruit, oats, and almonds. Prepare a Brand-Product Matrix from the above information and elaborate on the brand architecture strategy adopted by Coca-Cola

subject: Brand Management
text: Phool.co, an Indian social enterprise founded by Ankit Agarwal in 2017, is dedicated to sustainable, eco-friendly products made from floral waste collected from temples. With a mission to address the pollution caused by floral offerings disposed in rivers, Phool repurposes these flowers into premium incense sticks, cones, and vermicompost. Its product portfolio includes natural, charcoal-free incense sticks branded as "Flute," scented cones, and “Fleather,” a vegan leather alternative. Phool’s products are handmade, biodegradable, and feature floral fragrances like jasmine, rose, and sandalwood. The brand focuses on environmental impact and empowering local women, creating dignified livelihoods in its workforce. Phool's advertising leverages social media and eco-conscious influencers to highlight its sustainable practices and social impact, resonating with environmentally aware consumers. This innovative approach has garnered Phool international recognition, including support from the United Nations and partnerships with global retail brands promoting eco- friendly lifestyles. Suggest an Integrated Marketing Communication Plan for rural expansion in India. How should the plan be customised for rural markets.

text: Mr. V G Siddhartha is now virtually the coffee king of India? He is the Chairman of the Bangalore-based Amalgamated Bean Coffee Trading Co. (ABC) and is the man behind India’s largest coffee chain, Café Coffee Day (CCD). On October 11, 2011 Siddhartha was awarded as the Next Gen Entrepreneur award by Forbes India. But this was not a cake-walk for Siddhartha. From setting up its 1st cafe outlet in 1996 on Brigade Road in Bangalore, CCD is now bubbling with 1232 stores and counting, with another 6 stores outside India in Vienna and Karachi. Your brand is more than your logo, name or slogan — it’s the entire experience your prospects and customers have with your company, product and service. This is where CCD pulled a master stroke of changing the whole calculus of coffee consumption in a tea drinking country like India. Belonging to a coffee plantation family Siddhartha was quick to capitalize on the advantage of having an estate of coffee shrubs rolling over 10,000 acres. Taking a leaf out of South East Asia’s strategy (beer instead of coffee), Siddhartha started serving free ps coffee to whoever came to his internet café. This was just the stepping stone, where he used internet just as bait for the people. It was all part of a strategy of convincing customers not that they liked coffee, but liked the fact that they are holding and sipping a coffee. fs With its vision to be the friendly and stylish social hub for the young and the free spirited to get together and converse over a cup of coffee, and complementing this is the fact that half of India having being born after 1983,the company rightly calls itself “India’s largest youth aggregator.” And with their simple yet sensitive objective “A great cup of coffee. From bean, to cup. Every time”, they have hit the right notes. Having zeroed in on the youth and the young at heart as the target market, CCD is just the place away from home or office where you can relax all by yourself or with others. Over the years CCD has undergone total café rebranding, with jumping to an all new ‘smart? menu for in-house and take away food, changes in ultra-comfort furniture design and seating, new uniforms, cutlery. These changes are designed to facilitate a more interactive in-café experience for customers and enhanced customer service. CCD has created a friendly, clean and sober café environment that offers affordable and excellent range of products, being an essential part of everyone’s lifestyle: New entrance in the Indian coffee market of the global coffee giant, Seattle- headquartered, Starbucks teaming up with the Indian mega conglomerate, the Tata Group does pose a challenge for CCD. CCD has definitely connected well with coffee lovers as we are seeing higher growth in cafés. Café Coffee Day has played an essential role in awakening India to the coffee café culture by giving people an enjoyable ambience, from cozy seating to ordering the finest selections of coffee brews, beverages and food. And above all, it has given a place where India could go and spend a while to think and talk about things they like. Please comment on the unique success journey so far of Café Coffee Day in terms of Brand Management. In lieu of the competition ahead, what changes can CCD make to its Brand Management strategies?
